## Summary

- classify review findings separately by severity and scope disposition: `FIX_IN_PR`, `FOLLOW_UP`, or `HUMAN_DECISION`
- restrict synthesis action items and `FIX_PR` recommendations to bounded `FIX_IN_PR` work
- stop orchestration after one automatic fix pass or before scope-expanding work
- require fix-pr runs to preserve the original acceptance criteria and leave broader hardening for follow-up

## Scope

Intentionally limited to the four prompts that control review, synthesis, orchestration, and PR fixes. This PR does not add runtime machinery, workflow changes, documentation, or release notes.

## Verification

- `npm --prefix .agent run build`
- `npm --prefix .agent run check:docs`
- `git diff --check`

## Notes

- The severity/disposition separation is consistently established across review, synthesis, orchestration, and fix-pr prompts.
- The only in-scope blocker is the self-approval handoff loophole. Its smallest correction is confined to `agent-orchestrator.md`.
- `Keep docs in sync` was not scored: explicit maintainer direction makes runtime, workflow, test, and documentation changes follow-up-only for this PR.

## Findings

- **BLOCKING — FIX_IN_PR — Separate decision gates from action authorization:** After one completed automatic fix pass, a later review can route through `HUMAN_DECISION` to self-approval, whose `REQUEST_CHANGES` result still mandates another `fix-pr` handoff. That context also is not required to carry the new `FIX_IN_PR` classification. Qualify the self-approval branch with the same current-chain fix budget and require bounded `FIX_IN_PR` context; otherwise stop for human review.
- **INFO — FOLLOW_UP:** Deterministic runtime enforcement, regression tests, workflow changes, and documentation could strengthen this policy, but must remain outside this four-prompt PR.

## Final Rubric Verdict

PARTIAL

## AI Review Synthesis > Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**. > Requested by @lolipopshock. ## Summary of PR/Issue PR #498 introduces separate severity and scope-disposition classifications across the four prompts governing review, synthesis, orchestration, and PR fixes. Its goal is to prevent automated review loops from expanding a PR beyond its acceptance criteria. Runtime, workflow, test, documentation, and release-note changes are intentionally excluded. The current diff is surgical and CI passes, but several prompt clauses still contradict the new contract. ## Review The current head should not merge yet. Although one reviewer recommended shipping, the Codex and rubric reviews identified contract-breaking paths that remain present at `aa0a2209`, including a second automatic fix pass through self-approval. | Issue | Severity | Description | | -- | -- | -- | | Self-approval bypasses the one-pass circuit breaker | BLOCKING | The budget check covers review-to-fix handoffs, but an unconditional self-approval `REQUEST_CHANGES` handoff can start a second automatic fix pass. This directly violates the PR’s stated one-pass contract. | | Selected fix task is not exclusive | BLOCKING | The fix prompt calls orchestrator context the selected task, then reauthorizes work from the latest synthesis. This can revive `FIX_IN_PR` items deliberately omitted from the bounded handoff. | | Severity overrides disposition downstream | BLOCKING | The fixer and orchestrator categorically exclude `INFO` findings, so an `INFO` / `FIX_IN_PR` correction is discarded despite severity and disposition being declared independent. | | Action-item disposition is lost during handoff | WARNING | Synthesis permits unlabeled checkboxes while downstream prompts require explicit `FIX_IN_PR` classification; the existing extractor forwards only the checkbox text. | | `HUMAN_DECISION` routing is ambiguous | WARNING | Synthesis defines it as needing a maintainer, while orchestration sends it to agent self-approval, and no precedence is defined when both `HUMAN_DECISION` and `FIX_IN_PR` work remain. | | Recommendation parser shares disposition vocabulary | INFO | The `NO_AUTOMATED_ACTION` description embeds `HUMAN_DECISION`, while the parser selects the first recognized token. The prescribed output order keeps this bounded and fail-safe, so hardening can remain follow-up work. | ## Progress - The current head remains `aa0a22091ae0c7bd6491697f571ae488dbb03afa`; the hosted `check` job passes. - The diff remains limited to the four intended prompt files, with no release-note changes. - The existing rubric review already documents the self-approval loophole, so no duplicate inline comment was posted for it. - Posted three missing inline comments covering [selected-task exclusivity](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/498#discussion_r3771642157), [severity overriding disposition](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/498#discussion_r3771642161), and [lost action-item classification](https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/pull/498#discussion_r3771642158). - No pre-existing inline comments or review threads required replies, resolution, or minimization. - Deterministic runtime enforcement, heuristics-mode behavior, tests, documentation, and the sibling finalize prompt remain intentionally outside this PR. ## Issue Details
Self-approval bypasses the one-pass circuit breaker **Cause:** The new history check applies only before review-to-`fix-pr`, while the later self-approval rule unconditionally maps `REQUEST_CHANGES` to `fix-pr`. **Candidate solutions:** Apply the same completed-pass and disposition checks before every automated `fix-pr` handoff. After one completed pass, self-approval should stop for human review. **Comments:** The Codex and rubric reviewers independently identified this path. The shipping reviewer treated the budget as advisory but did not account for this concrete bypass.
Selected fix task is not exclusive **Cause:** The priority list makes non-empty orchestrator context the selected fix task, but the authorization rule allows work from that context “or latest synthesis.” **Candidate solutions:** When orchestrator context is present, make it the exclusive authorization source. Consult synthesis action items only when no selected context exists.
Severity overrides disposition downstream **Cause:** Blanket `INFO` exclusions in the fixer and orchestrator override the independently assigned `FIX_IN_PR` disposition. **Candidate solutions:** Let disposition determine automation eligibility. Exclude optional or `FOLLOW_UP` INFO findings, not every INFO finding. **Comments:** This is a direct counterexample to the otherwise well-established severity/disposition separation noted by the other reviewers.
Action-item disposition is lost during handoff **Cause:** The synthesis format requires only plain checkboxes, and `extractReviewActionItems` forwards their text without recovering the table disposition. **Candidate solutions:** Require a literal format such as `- [ ] FIX_IN_PR: …`. The existing extractor will preserve that label without runtime changes.
HUMAN_DECISION routing is ambiguous **Cause:** Its definition says a maintainer is required, but existing orchestration intentionally uses agent self-approval as the judgment gate. The next-step predicates also overlap when decision work and branch fixes coexist. **Candidate solutions:** Define `HUMAN_DECISION` as an explicit judgment gate consistent with self-approval, and give it precedence whenever that decision must occur before branch changes.
Recommendation parser shares disposition vocabulary **Cause:** `extractReviewRecommendedNextStep` returns the first recognized token in the section, while explanatory text may mention sibling next-step tokens. **Candidate solutions:** As follow-up hardening, require the selected token on its own first line or avoid sibling next-step tokens in its explanation. **Comments:** The prescribed format already places the selected token first, and the plausible misroute stops at a judgment gate rather than triggering unsafe automation.
## Recommended Next Step `FIX_PR`: the unresolved contract contradictions require a bounded prompt-only correction and are safe for one automated fix pass within the four changed files. ## Final Verdict `NEEDS_REWORK` ## Action Items - [ ] FIX_IN_PR: Apply the one-pass budget and bounded-disposition checks to every automated `fix-pr` handoff, including self-approval. - [ ] FIX_IN_PR: Make non-empty orchestrator context the exclusive fix authorization source. - [ ] FIX_IN_PR: Make disposition—not severity—the downstream actionability gate. - [ ] FIX_IN_PR: Require explicit `FIX_IN_PR` labels in synthesis action-item checkboxes. - [ ] FIX_IN_PR: Align `HUMAN_DECISION` terminology with the configured judgment gate and define precedence for mixed dispositions. --- `codex` | `gpt-5.6-sol[max]` | `Macmini-runner-5`

Task for fix-pr:
Address only the latest review synthesis action items in one bounded pass, modifying strictly the four prompt files already changed by PR #498: (1) apply the one-pass budget and bounded-disposition checks to every automated fix-pr handoff, including self-approval; (2) make non-empty orchestrator context the exclusive fix authorization source; (3) make disposition—not severity—the downstream actionability gate; (4) require explicit FIX_IN_PR labels in synthesis action-item checkboxes; and (5) align HUMAN_DECISION terminology with the configured judgment gate and define precedence for mixed dispositions. Preserve the stated scope-disposition contract. Ignore optional INFO notes, metadata-only polish, already-fixed findings, and human-judgment nits unless required by those five items. Do not add or modify runtime, workflow, test, documentation, or broader hardening changes; if any required resolution would need such expansion, stop for human review.

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #498 updates four prompts governing review, synthesis, orchestration, and PR fixes. It separates finding severity from scope disposition so valid concerns do not automatically expand a pull request. It also limits automation to one bounded fix pass and preserves the original acceptance criteria. The current head includes the requested prompt-only corrections without runtime, workflow, test, documentation, or release-note changes.

## Review

All three current-head reviews converge on SHIP/PASS with no unresolved `FIX_IN_PR` or `HUMAN_DECISION` work. Remaining runtime enforcement and heuristics-mode concerns are explicitly out-of-scope follow-ups.

- Claude described several runtime follow-ups individually, while Codex and the rubric review summarized them together; all agree they are non-blocking and outside this prompt-only scope.
- Marked three superseded same-agent inline comments as outdated after re-verifying authorship, PR ownership, and the corrected current-head text.
- No new inline comments, replies, or thread resolutions were needed.

`NO_AUTOMATED_ACTION`: no required branch changes remain, and another fix pass would violate the one-pass scope contract.
